headline: session-continue.sh blocks a stop in 5 cases, all by printing decision:block and exiting 0: the ship floor on a 📦 rung (L1187/1199, off with CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0), the ship floor on a 🚀 rung (L1189/1199, same switch), the wake floor (L894-895, off with CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0), the mechanical 🔧 arm that ends in a continuation block (L1072-1080 then L1334/1336, off with CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0), and an armed sentinel continuation (L1334/1336), which has no env switch and is escaped only by `clear`, a kill phrase, or the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop in 5 cases. Two go through the continuation sentinel, which blocks at lines 1334/1336. Case 1 is a sentinel armed with `set`; it is disabled by `clear`, a sid mismatch or `CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX`. Case 2 is the mechanical 🔧 arm for this session's own uncommitted files; it is disabled by `CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0` or `CC_MECH_MAX`. The other three are floors that apply when no sentinel is armed. Cases 3 and 4 are the ship floor (line 1199) for 📦 unlanded commits and 🚀 not-live work; they are disabled by `CC_SHIP_FLOOR` other than 1 or `CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX`. Case 5 is the wake floor (line 895) for going idle with no inbox watcher armed; it is disabled by `CC_WAKE_FLOOR` other than 1 or `CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX`. An operator kill phrase (`KILL_RE`, line 348) turns off all five.

The session-continue.sh Stop hook blocks a stop under 4 conditions, each by emitting decision:block JSON with exit 0: the armed-sentinel continuation (lines 1334/1336; operator kill phrase, clear or the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap), the mechanical 🔧 arm for this session's uncommitted files (armed at 1072, same emit; CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0), the ship floor (1199; CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0) and the wake floor (894-895; CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0).

The Stop hook blocks under 5 conditions: an agent-set sentinel (line 1334/1336, capped by CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX), the mechanical arm for this session's uncommitted writes (same lines; off with CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0), the ship floor for the 📦 and 🚀 rungs (line 1199; off with CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0), and the wake floor (line 895; off with CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0). A kill-switch phrase in the last user message stops all of them.

rotate-logs.sh has 6 real bugs: the worst is that nothing checks `cd $dir` (line 5), so line 11 can delete .gz files in the wrong directory. Line 11 also keeps only keep-1 archives, splits names on whitespace before `rm` and deletes every .gz rather than only log archives; `-mtime +1` (line 7) means 2 days, and the ls loop and unquoted test (lines 6-7) break on unusual file names.

rotate-logs.sh has 7 real bugs; the worst is that nothing checks whether `cd $dir` (unquoted) worked, so a missing directory or argument makes it gzip and delete files in the current directory or $HOME. Next: the `tail -n +$keep` off-by-one keeps only keep-1 archives, `*.gz` deletes unrelated archives, xargs and `$(ls)` split filenames on spaces, `-mtime +1` really means 2 or more days, and gzip fails when an archive with the same name already exists.

rotate-logs.sh has 6 real bugs: the worst is an unchecked `cd` that can gzip logs and delete archives in the wrong directory, then an off-by-one in `tail -n +$keep` that keeps one archive too few, then unsafe whitespace handling in `xargs rm`, `-mtime +1` meaning at least 2 days old, word-splitting of filenames in the loop and test, and gzip failing when an earlier archive of the same name exists.

The others: an off-by-one in `tail -n +$keep` keeps one archive too few, gzip skips any log whose .gz name already exists, word splitting in the loop and `[ $(find) ]` test, xargs breaking on whitespace in names, and a `-mtime +1` test that only matches files 48 or more hours old.
